raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Request for bank earnings-call data and forward guidance on AT1 costs",
  "main_topics": ["current account balances", "AT1 costs", "financing businesses"],
  "answer_completeness": "Partial",
  "response_stance": "Hedged",
  "evidence_level": "Medium",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": false,
  "contains_forward_guidance": true,
  "narrative_alignment": "Partially aligned",
  "question_quote": "Two questions. One, just quickly on some numbers you may or may not be able to give us, but just the average current account balances. And those are, I guess, period end. So how different do they look like on a sort of intra-month average versus end of the month just as people have been paid? And how much lower would the median be than the average on this? And then secondly, you've talked about AT1 costs being sort of a hurdle rate for returns on the leveraged balance sheets in FICC Financing and in Prime. Do you think about that across customer relationships? Obviously, let's say, an institution using repo and prime, do you aggregate the two to think about the hurdle? Or do you think about it specifically within FICC on one side, Prime on the other? And then your AT1s are just, it's a very low hurdle rate right now, right? AT1, let's say, 5% to 6%. So that's obviously not the hurdle rate you think about managing the group towards. So how much would you sort of be willing perhaps to work on that AT1 hurdle rate compromising your group return, but maintaining market share, etc, within the financing businesses?",
  "answer_quote": "Why don't I start of on that? I'm not going to be able to give you all the numbers that you want but let me help you think about it. And then I will invite Dan to make some comments on AT1 costs. So, remember, there are two types of current accounts that we think about in the Group, and they actually move differently. So, in retail, customers get paid at the beginning of the month. And then typically, what happens is they start paying their bills, their mortgages, etc, balances drop of quite quickly. So, you get an intra-month loan. Corporates are exactly the opposite. So pre-Barclays UK, when we used to have something called Personal and Corporate Bank (PCB), which some of you will remember, the current account balances were actually relatively stable because you have these two waves going in opposite directions. That makes sense. You're right, in retail, there is that intra-month dip, but there is the opposite in Corporate. And to a lesser extent, Business Banking, it's not quite extreme. But we don't disclose the sort of top to bottom drop in either of those. And obviously, they sit in different legal entities. Dan, why don't you talk about AT1 costs, and then I'll pick up how we think about the financing relationship. Yes. I mean exactly right. We do look at the AT1 cost, and we use it as a hurdle rate for the returns we would expect to get in the Financing business. We don't really think about it on a coupon level. We would always need to have the total capital level anyway. So, the way we think about it really is the spread differential between AT1 and Tier 2 because we weren't issuing more AT1 than we need, we would be issuing Tier 2 instead. So that's the way that we think about it. In terms of sort of analysing the hurdle return for the business, just from a simplicity perspective, I think about it is that we should be clearing that return in our lowest returning bits of the complex. So extremely liquid fixed income where you've got the very highest quality government securities, that's generally the lowest margin business. We should be returning more than the cost of AT1 in that business and it's extremely liquid. So we've got a high degree of confidence that we can move it around. We would expect that the client return is obviously higher than that because if we're dealing with a client, they'll be dealing across multiple products and they are clearly profitable, then we are comfortable overall. And the last thing I would say is we do think about the clients as a single client across both platforms. So, as we deal with them, as we look at them, as we risk manage them, we are looking at them across Fixed Income Financing and Prime together. And that's really important if you like, the strategy of that part of the franchise. So, I think that probably brings us to the end. Thank you very much for coming in. Really appreciate your time. Really appreciate your interest in Barclays. We will see you in an expectingly short period of time because this is the shortest quarter. So, we'll see you at Q1 very, very soon. And until then, stay well. Thank you.",
  "reason": "The answer provides partial information on current account balances and AT1 costs, but does not give the specific numbers requested. It also discusses the strategy of considering clients across both platforms, which is partially aligned with the question's intent but does not directly address the comparison of intra-month averages and end-of-month balances or the specific willingness to work on AT1 hurdle rates."
}
